purpose: Machine-readable index of every claim this repository makes, with its evidence. Validated by test/test-findings.js, which checks the numbers against the same library the suites use, checks that each registering commit precedes its results commit, and checks that each named test file exists and mentions the finding.

outcome_values.HELD: Registered as a prediction before the run, and the run confirmed it.
outcome_values.FAILED: Registered as a prediction before the run, and the run refuted it. Kept, not corrected away.
outcome_values.MEASURED_NOT_REGISTERED: Measured during design rather than predicted. Listed separately so the pre-registration record is not inflated by facts that were never at risk.

prediction_sets.subject: What the TGATE control vocabulary generates

predictions.claim: addi saturates at exactly 3^w
the full control vocabulary saturates rather than growing freely
reach(all, w) = reach(all, 1)^w, a direct product across trit positions
predictions.note: The failure produced the real law. One composition step applies one control to ALL positions, so after d steps every position carries a word of length exactly d; the positions must agree on word LENGTH, which is weaker than a direct product. reach(w) = |union over d of (M_d)^w|, validated on five widths before being used at width 6.

predictions.claim: more controls buy elements here, unlike table-audit's wide16
reach(all, 6) is not 531441
the shift vocabulary saturates

prediction_sets.subject: What TOP buys, once the truth table is data

predictions.claim: TOP with the second operand pinned reaches 27 at every width
predictions.note: 19,683 tables collapse to 27 maps: one column is in play, so every position gets the same map.

predictions.claim: pinned TOP reaches fewer elements than TGATE for width >= 2
TOP with a free second operand reaches exactly 27^w
predictions.note: And it explains why P3 failed: TOP can express the IDENTITY as a column, so positions idle while others advance, dissolving the equal-word-length constraint. TGATE has no identity mode.

predictions.claim: 27^w is the ceiling for any positionwise vocabulary
the width-6 ceiling 27^6 exceeds 531441
the positionwise vocabulary saturates at exactly 27^w
27 more positionwise generators reach the same number
one translation exceeds 27^w at width 2 by at least 10x
one shift also escapes at width 2
the escape is cross-trit coupling, not generator count
predictions.note: Not all coupling is equal, and this was NOT predicted: the carry buys 3,483x what the shift does, because a carry is data-dependent and a shift is a fixed relabelling.

prediction_sets.subject: Folding a chain of TOP tables into one

predictions.claim: an N-stage chain folds to one instruction, saving (N-1) stages
predictions.note: Held, with an accounting correction: S1 was written in STAGES, and each stage is six instructions, so the saving reads as 18-20 instructions rather than 3. The prose in the first run also mis-rendered this line before it was cleaned up.

predictions.claim: the saving multiplies with emulation depth
hash-consing pays exactly 9 cells per duplicate table
the fold does not survive a carry

prediction_sets.subject: TOPC, the carry as a table

predictions.claim: no TOP table equals ADD, over all 19683, compared as functions
predictions.note: The 81 is the point: a single-point comparison would have reported 81 false matches.

predictions.claim: positionwise + TOPC carrying ADD reaches 251505 at width 2
TOPC in the core would end depth 4

prediction_sets.subject: Whether the ceiling ladder has another rung

predictions.claim: at width 1 the carry is inert; TOPC reaches 27 like TOP
at width 2 TOPC alone exceeds the 729 ceiling
arbitrary carries reach more than the 251505 that ADD alone reaches
predictions.note: The first run reported this as FAILED. It had not failed: at depth 16 the sampled vocabulary was still growing while the ADD one had closed, so a smaller number was read as a smaller reach. The auditor now distinguishes closed, capped and depth-exhausted, and a test asserts all three stay distinguishable.

predictions.claim: the sample is a lower bound and no upper bound is claimed

prediction_sets.subject: The switch-level device layer beneath the arithmetic

predictions.claim: six per-trit gates side by side compute the six-trit function, exhaustively
gates compose: a pass network driving a pass network does not degrade
predictions.note: The first run reported this FAILED. The circuit was correct; the SOLVER was wrong -- reachability traversed through rails, so correct circuits resolved to X. Driven nodes are terminals now. Second time an instrument here produced a false verdict on its own prediction; the first was V3.

predictions.claim: at equal representable range the naive switch count favours ternary, and should not be believed
predictions.note: The ternary side taps a third rail this model hands out free; real ternary logic must generate its mid level with dividers that burn static power. Switch count per gate is also a different currency from the 3.08x per-digit bar.

prediction_sets.subject: The axioms the switch-level device model rests on

predictions.claim: the inclusive threshold (D3) is load-bearing: strict thresholds break every gate
predictions.note: The row counts were derived by hand and written into the registration before the run. They were right. On this integer domain a strict n(t) is an inclusive n(t+1), and a device that can never conduct is indistinguishable from an absent one, so the mutation is a transformation of the device list rather than a patch to the solver.

predictions.claim: the fixed point is not unique, and an all-X start is indistinguishable from all-Z
predictions.note: FAILED on its premise, not its answer. It asked which seeds of the self-inverter are self-consistent, taking for granted that every seed resolves to something. Two of three do not: seeded at a level the network runs -1 -> +1 -> -1 forever and solve() throws. That falsified N7, which claimed resolution cannot oscillate, full stop -- true only from the all-Z start, where any node with a non-driven gate goes to X on the first pass and stays. N7 was reworded to say so. The second half of X2 held exactly: 0 of 27 rows differ, because conducts() maps Z and X alike to unknown.

predictions.claim: composition (T3) holds for every wiring, not just the one already tested
the series mid path is not redundant: no single device can replace it

measured.why_six_not_twelve: D4 -- terminals are interchangeable, checked here rather than assumed

predictions.claim: four switches is minimal for NEG in this model
predictions.note: The positive control first reported the standard ternary inverter ABSENT from a search that had in fact found it: the network key ordered its terminals, and D4 says terminals have no order. Third time an instrument here produced a false verdict on its own prediction. V3 and W2 were the others.

unregistered_findings.claim: ADD equals TOPC with the 27-row addition table, exactly.
An interpreter bug that permutes the emulated semantics has an ORDER, and is invisible at layer counts divisible by it. Order 2 is masked at 2 layers; order 3 at 3.
unregistered_findings.consequence: No single depth is a safe place to test; the acceptance tests compare every depth.

unregistered_findings.claim: Folding buys a level of emulation depth, not just instructions: the unfolded chain is refused at depth 4 and the folded one runs.
TGATE's three modes are not closed under composition: 6 of its 8 two-stage composites are not any TGATE mode. This is why TOP folds and TGATE cannot.
Reading -1/0/+1 as false/unknown/true, MIN, MAX and NEG are exactly the connectives of Kleene's strong three-valued logic. Excluded middle and non-contradiction both fail at unknown.
unregistered_findings.precision: For these three connectives K3 and Lukasiewicz's L3 are identical; they diverge only at implication, which this machine has no operator for.

unregistered_findings.claim: Base 3 is the cheapest integer radix by the radix-economy measure: representing a million values costs 40 in base 2, 39 in base 3, 40 in base 4.

Three-way dispatch beats two-way on the same machine by about half an instruction and a fifth of the code per decision point, and nothing at all when the decision is genuinely binary. Deep dispatch loses outright to an indexed jump: 149 cells against 30.

The top rung of the ladder is 531,441, numerically identical to the source conversation's figure, by coincidence. That figure counted two-stage configurations of 6-trit trytes (729^2); this counts elements of a monoid on 9 points (9^6). Both are 3^12 for unrelated reasons, and the conversation's claim about what it counted remains wrong.
The standard ternary inverter computes NEG on all three inputs; MIN and MAX are correct on all nine rows. Switch counts: STI 4, NTI 2, PTI 2, MIN 8, MAX 8.
unregistered_findings.note: Established while designing the gates, so not registered as a prediction.

unregistered_findings.claim: The standard ternary inverter is not the only four-switch NEG in this model. Exhaustive search finds four distinct networks, and it is one of them.
unregistered_findings.evidence: 148,995 four-switch networks over 42 device types, all solved

traps_encountered.description: Comparing two functions at a single input and concluding they are equal. Bit the mixed-TGATE test, the folded-vs-unfolded programs, and the TOP-vs-ADD comparison, where 81 of 19,683 tables matched at one pair.
A hardcoded count in a test going stale when the thing it counted grew. The closure test's opcode list, and several depth-window numbers. Both now derive their values.
Writing through a missing label produced an undefined address, so the write silently did nothing. The core interpreter ran with no control register and no complaint.
.fold reading nine cells from a table that was shorter, silently borrowing whatever followed it.
Reading depth exhaustion as saturation, which produced a false FAILED verdict for V3.

Switch-level reachability traversing THROUGH a driven node. A path from one rail that touches another rail and continues out of it makes correct circuits look contended. Rails and inputs are ideal sources and must terminate a path.

The measuring tool, not the thing measured, producing the failure. V3 read depth exhaustion as saturation; W2 traversed reachability through rails; X5 keyed a network by ordered terminals when D4 says terminals have no order. Each reported FAILED or ABSENT for something that was fine. Check the shape of an answer before believing its verdict.

A prediction failing on an assumption it never stated rather than on the quantity it asked about. X2 asked which seeds are self-consistent and assumed every seed resolves; two do not. The assumption, not the answer, was the falsifiable part.
